intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: The news article states the 1 December 1968 groundbreaking was for the linac, the first part of the accelerator complex. No completion date sourced.
intervals.quote: the lab broke ground for its first accelerator on Dec. 1, 1968.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Evidence date, not a commissioning date: this is the earliest operation of the machine documented by a source fetched in this session (NuMI beam paper, MINOS data taking from 20 May 2005). The machine has run since the 1970s; no fetchable source gave its commissioning date (fnal.gov and history.fnal.gov returned HTTP 403).
intervals.quote: Protons originate as H - ions in the Linac which accelerates them to 400 MeV.

start.display: in operation by 2005; commissioning date not sourced

beam_energy.quote: Subsequently a 201.2 MHz linac accelerates them to 400 MeV

summary.plain: The first machine in the Fermilab chain: it turns hydrogen ions into a 400-million-electronvolt beam and passes them to the next accelerator.
summary.technical: 201.25 MHz normal-conducting H- linac delivering 400 MeV to the Booster; to be replaced by the 800 MeV PIP-II superconducting linac.
